evidence.title: Getting started with Cosmos
evidence.finding: Cosmos runs Experts in sandboxed VMs with triggers, private/shared sessions and persistent automation rules.

evidence.title: Augment Code homepage
evidence.locator: Start from anything; run anywhere; humans; memory
evidence.finding: The vendor advertises managed and user-owned execution, shared memory, expert handoffs and human checkpoints. These claims were not exercised.

evidence.title: Introducing Auggie CLI
evidence.finding: The 1.x docs describe a prerelease CLI requiring Node 20+, account login, local indexing and print/stream/JSON automation modes.

evidence.title: Augment pricing
evidence.locator: Plan cards; usage FAQ checked 7 November 2026
evidence.finding: Standard and Business are flat team prices with pooled dollar usage; LLM API list price has a 40% service fee and compute is separate.

evidence.title: Augment changelog
evidence.finding: Release notes state agents no longer merge PRs, session cost visibility is admin-only, snapshots last fourteen days, and analytics can export CSV.

evidence.title: Augment Code homepage
evidence.locator: Title; Harness announcement banner; PR Author; footer
evidence.finding: The page retains the Augment Code name, links the Harness announcement and credits Harness, Inc. in its footer. PR Author is described as driving work through merge without naming who executes the merge.

evidence.title: Augment Code's next chapter
evidence.finding: Augment agreed to sell selected assets, including Cosmos, Auggie CLI and the Code Context Engine, to Harness. The team behind those products is moving to Harness to continue their development.

evidence.title: Harness acquires Augment Code to advance the Autonomous SDLC
evidence.locator: Published 8 October 2026, updated 19 October; acquisition; What makes Harness Cosmos; Get started
evidence.finding: Harness says it acquired selected Augment assets, names Cosmos the Harness Cosmos Software Factory Agent and says it is available now. Agents prepare changes for a team merge decision.

evidence.title: Cosmos Software Factory Agent - Ticket to Code
evidence.locator: Product heading; idea to merge-ready code; Start for free
evidence.finding: Harness lists Cosmos Software Factory Agent as a current product and links to cosmos.augmentcode.com. Its stated output is merge-ready code.

evidence.title: PR to Merge
evidence.locator: How it works; Where you participate
evidence.finding: Experts review and repair changes. A human decides and performs the final merge. Configured agent approval is separate from merging.

evidence.title: PR Author
evidence.finding: PR Author creates a branch, implements the change, opens a PR or MR and handles CI, merge conflicts and review comments.

evidence.title: Cosmos Week 38 Release Notes
evidence.finding: The release note explicitly removes agent pull-request merging.

evidence.title: Harness acquires Augment Code to advance the Autonomous SDLC
evidence.locator: Connecting code context; From a downstream finding; Bringing governance
evidence.finding: Planned work connects code and delivery context, downstream verification feedback, and Harness governance controls. No shipment date is stated.

evidence.title: Using Sessions
evidence.locator: About sessions; Session lifecycle; Share a session
evidence.finding: Cosmos supports phone browsers, explicitly has no separate iOS/Android app, saves conversations indefinitely, and gives individually shared users viewer access. Environments pause and may restart clean.

evidence.title: Using Tasklist
evidence.locator: Creating a New Task; Subtasks; Status; Reviewing Changes
evidence.finding: IDE Tasklist supports human and agent creation, editable nested tasks, explicit execution, state indicators, moving lists to a new chat and per-task diff review.

evidence.title: Project Builder
evidence.finding: The Expert drafts a design, iterates with the human, breaks work into tickets and launches PR Author workers in dependency waves. It never writes implementation code or merges.

evidence.title: Auggie Subagents
evidence.finding: Built-in and custom subagents have independent context, tools and prompts, run concurrently and report progress in the parent thread. Configuration includes model and thinking level.

evidence.title: Daemon Workspaces and Isolation
evidence.finding: Isolated daemon sessions get one Git worktree per repository. Shared sessions edit the daemon checkout and may overwrite each other. Isolation requires Git 2.31+.

evidence.title: Install Auggie CLI
evidence.finding: Auggie runs locally or on a server with Node 20+, macOS, Linux or Windows WSL and zsh/bash/fish. Version 1 is prerelease; stable 0.x remains available.

evidence.title: PR Author
evidence.finding: PR Author creates branches and pull or merge requests, follows CI, handles merge conflicts and responds to review comments.

evidence.title: Using Teams
evidence.finding: Administrator manages invites, members, seats, plan and billing. Member can view team information or leave, but cannot administer billing or membership.

evidence.title: Augment Code Pricing
evidence.locator: Plan cards; Usage FAQ; Support FAQ
evidence.finding: Standard is $20/month for up to 50 seats with $20 shared usage; Business is $100. LLM list rates plus 40% service fee, compute without that fee, pooled top-ups valid twelve months. Trials exclude SLA.

evidence.title: Available Models
evidence.finding: Augment lists Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, Zhipu, xAI and Moonshot models, subject to organization configuration; model options do not prove external harness support.

evidence.title: Augment Code introduction.md
evidence.locator: Cosmos, Auggie CLI, IDE clients; linked current model/subagent documentation
evidence.finding: The introduction distinguishes the Cosmos automation product, Auggie CLI and Augment IDE clients. The coding workflow is supplied by Augment/Auggie and Cosmos experts; selected Anthropic/OpenAI/Google/xAI model providers do not run those vendors coding CLI harnesses.

evidence.title: Augment Code professional terms of service
evidence.finding: The main software-engineering AI platform is covered by Augment professional terms. Customer access is non-exclusive/non-transferable and limited to internal business use; distribution, reverse engineering and derivative versions are restricted, and the company retains platform intellectual property.

evidence.title: Augment Code pricing
evidence.locator: Public plan cards; Usage, top-up and trial FAQ
evidence.finding: The complete current public plans are paid Standard $20/month, Business $100/month and custom Enterprise. Standard/Business pool model/context/compute dollar usage; top-ups are usage based. Trials have separate support terms, with no recurring free tier listed. No BYOK or one-time purchase plan is listed.

desktop-os:macos, desktop-os:windows, desktop-os:linux: Primary Cosmos client is hosted web; companion Auggie CLI platform support does not establish a native primary desktop app.

byo-subscription: The closed product documents Augment authentication and metered model usage, but no explicit native Claude/ChatGPT coding-agent subscription reuse guarantee or restriction.
isolation:container: Cloud VMs and self-hosted daemon worktrees are established, but container-per-agent isolation is not established by those findings.
multiplayer: Sharing grants viewer access. It does not establish other users prompting, and the closed service has no explicit negative contract for all session roles.
telemetry-opt-out: Data/training policies do not establish a documented ADE telemetry-disable control.

self-hosting: Official daemons provide self-managed execution workers connected to Cosmos. A self-hostable whole control plane is not established or explicitly ruled out by the public closed-service terms.
